question.problem:
A website has a $12%$ chance of crashing during a peak traffic test. The test is run $10$ times. Rounded to $3$ decimal places, what is the probability that the site crashes at least $2$ times?

Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be equal to the number of times the site crashes.

Here, we have the following information:

- There are $n=10$ tests.

- The probability of a crash is $p=12%=0.12.$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(10,0.12).$

The number of successes of a binomial random variable has the probability mass function

$$
P(X=x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x},
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments, and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

Substituting the above information into the formula for the probability mass function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=x) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{10}{x})(0.12)^{x}(1-0.12)^{10-x} \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{10}{x})(0.12)^{x}(0.88)^{10-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find the probability of at least $2$ crashes. This corresponds to $P(X\ge 2).$

However, computing

$$
P(X\ge 2)=P(X=2)+P(X=3)+…+P(X=10)
$$

will involve many computations, so let's express our answer in terms of the complement instead. By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 2) & =1-P(X<2) \\  & =1-[P(X=0)+P(X=1)] \\  & =1-[(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{10}{0})(0.12)^{0}(0.88)^{10-0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{10}{1})(0.12)^{1}(0.88)^{10-1}] \\  & =1-[(0.88)^{10}+10(0.12)(0.88)^{9}] \\  & =1-0.658\,275… \\  & ≈0.342,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
